title: Canonical graded twisting algebra on relative Proj of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ be a commutative unital graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra [def-trf-etale-graded-module-algebra] with each component quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and put $p:P=P_X(\mathcal A)\to X$ [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests]. Use small etale module sheaves, tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There are quasi-coherent modules $E_n=\mathcal O_P(n)$ for $n\in\mathbf Z$, with $E_0=\mathcal O_P$, unital associative ordinary commutative homogeneous products $E_m\otimes E_n\to E_{m+n}$, and a canonical graded unital map $\psi:p^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}E_n$. The sum denotes the coproduct of module sheaves. For every scheme $g:W\to X$, the scheme-test comparison identifies the pulled-back family, products and map with the ordinary relative-Proj twisting family and its canonical map [lem-sfb-relative-proj-twists-degree-opens] for $(g^*\mathcal A)_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. These comparisons commute with further scheme base change, identity and composition. In particular, if $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $C=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}(g^*\mathcal A_n)(W)$, then on $D_+(f)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}C$ for homogeneous $f\in C_d$, $d>0$, the Zariski module corresponding to $E_n$ is the sheaf associated to the $C_{(f)}$-module $(C_f)_n$, as in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. Products are multiplication of homogeneous fractions and $a\in C_n$ maps to $a/1$. The comparisons and these normalizations determine the family and map up to unique isomorphism preserving them. No finite generation, degree-one generation, flatness, separation or quasi-compactness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 084D (lemma-twists-of-structure-sheaf), with the twisting-algebra comparison of Tag 085C (lemma-relative-proj-base-change). Scheme and affine-chart normalization: constructions.tex Tag 01NR (lemma-glue-relative-proj-twists), using the affine twisting modules of def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf.

proof.text: Use tensor pullback throughout. By [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent], every degree of a pulled-back algebra is quasi-coherent. On schemes pass between Zariski and small etale modules by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Its forward functor is tensor pullback, so [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] identifies products on the two sites. The adjunction in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] show that pullback preserves the small coproducts indexed by $\mathbf N$ or $\mathbf Z$. Thus the comparison also identifies graded families and their total module sheaves. All composition comparisons below use [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition]: $c\otimes(d\otimes m)\mapsto c\,a^\sharp(d)\otimes m$. In particular their associativity follows by evaluating both parenthesizations on local tensors; after mapping all coefficients into the final structure ring, the two formulas are $((bc)d)\otimes m$ and $(b(cd))\otimes m$, and these are equal by associativity in that ring.

source.place: Tag 084D (lemma-twists-of-structure-sheaf), passage to scheme charts; sites-modules.tex Tags 03D7, 03D8, 03EL

proof.text: First form the scheme twisting data by [lem-sfb-relative-proj-twists-degree-opens]. For a scheme map $h:V\to Z$ and a graded quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal B$ on $Z$, cover $Z$ by affine opens $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $h^{-1}Z_0$ by affine opens $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}T$. Put $A=\bigoplus_j\mathcal B_j(Z_0)$ and $B=\bigoplus_j(h^*\mathcal B_j)(V_0)$. Degreewise [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identifies $B$ with $T\otimes_R A$, by $t\otimes a\mapsto t h^*a$; these maps preserve the algebra operations. The cartesian Proj map and covering standard opens are those of [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension]. This chart map $r_\psi$ is the base-change map of the scheme-test comparisons: by [lem-sfb-scheme-proj-veronese-quotient-functor] a map to a relative Proj is the class of the pulled-back universal datum $(d,\mathcal O(d),\text{canonical map})$, and the comparison $\theta^\psi_d$ below is an isomorphism $r_\psi^*\mathcal O(d)\simeq\mathcal O(d)$ carrying $a/1$ to $\psi(a)/1$, so (with the cartesian square for the maps to the base) $r_\psi$ and the functor-of-points base-change map classify equivalent data and coincide. On each inverse image $D_+(\psi(f))$, apply [lem-sfb-proj-scalar-extension-twist-comparison]: its degree-$j$ comparison is $(a/f^r)\otimes c\mapsto c\psi(a)/\psi(f)^r$. It is an isomorphism for every integer $j$ and preserves multiplication, the unit and homogeneous sections. These maps glue: they agree on standard-open intersections by that node's restriction compatibility, and on different affine base charts by the affine restriction comparisons of [lem-sfb-relative-proj-twists-degree-opens]. If two affine opens intersect, use affine opens inside the intersection, never an assumption that the intersection itself is affine. The sheaf condition glues both maps and their inverses. This gives a comparison of the entire twisting data for arbitrary scheme $h$.

source.place: Tag 01O3 (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), affine gluing via Tags 01N2 and 01NR

proof.text: Denote the scheme comparison just constructed by $\theta_h$. It is normalized in degree zero by the structure map. For composable scheme maps $V'\xrightarrow{k}V\xrightarrow{h}Z$, [lem-sfb-proj-scalar-extension-twist-comparison] gives $\theta_{hk}=\theta_k\circ k_P^*\theta_h$ on affine base charts, under the tensor-composition comparison; its identity comparison is the identity. These identities hold globally because the charts cover and maps of sheaves are equal if equal locally. The same formulas remain true when the pulled-back graded algebra is identified by its canonical graded isomorphism: on fractions the map is still $a/f^r\mapsto\psi(a)/\psi(f)^r$. Thus the identifications arising from two descriptions of the same pulled-back algebra are compatible with all subsequent pullbacks. By step 1 these statements hold also on the small etale sites. This proves the cocycle and section-map compatibility needed for descent, rather than assuming them from a bare existence of scheme twists.

Choose a scheme atlas $u:U\to X$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Set $U_2=U\times_XU$, $U_3=U\times_XU\times_XU$, and $P_V=V\times_XP$ for these scheme tests. These are schemes: the diagonal of $X$ is representable, and $P\to X$ is representable by schemes. By [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests], $P_V$ is the scheme relative Proj of $(\mathcal A|_V)_{\mathrm{Zar}}$, with compatible maps for the projections of $U_2,U_3$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $q:P_U\to P$ is surjective etale, $P_U\times_PP_U=P_{U_2}$, and its triple overlap is $P_{U_3}$. By [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus] this single-member covering is fppf, so effective module descent applies without requiring $q$ to be quasi-compact. Let $F_{V,n}$ and $\psi_V$ be the scheme twists and canonical map of step 2, viewed on the etale site. The scheme comparisons for the two projections $U_2\to U$ identify both pullbacks of $F_{U,n}$ with $F_{U_2,n}$. Their quotient is the descent isomorphism $\alpha_n:\operatorname{pr}_1^*F_{U,n}\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*F_{U,n}$. Step 3 gives $\alpha_{13}=\alpha_{23}\alpha_{12}$ on $P_{U_3}$ and the identity along the diagonal.

source.place: Tag 084D (lemma-twists-of-structure-sheaf), atlas and overlap construction, and the discussion after Tag 084C

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] separately to each $(F_{U,n},\alpha_n)$, $n\in\mathbf Z$. Obtain quasi-coherent modules $E_n$ and compatible isomorphisms $q^*E_n\simeq F_{U,n}$. In degree zero the normalized scheme comparisons are the canonical comparisons for $\mathcal O_P$, so full faithfulness identifies $E_0$ with $\mathcal O_P$; transport along this isomorphism to normalize $E_0=\mathcal O_P$. Tensor products of these modules are quasi-coherent: on a scheme chart use [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]; quasi-coherence is local by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. This also applies to repeated tensor products. Hence the full faithfulness in module descent can be used for all sources and targets of the algebra-law diagrams.

source.place: Tag 084D (lemma-twists-of-structure-sheaf), effectivity using spaces-descent.tex Tag 04W8; scheme tensor closure: Tag 01I8

proof.text: Under $q^*(E_m\otimes E_n)\simeq F_{U,m}\otimes F_{U,n}$, the multiplication of the scheme twists is a morphism of descent data, since both projection comparisons preserve multiplication (steps 2--3). By [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] it descends uniquely to $\mu_{m,n}:E_m\otimes E_n\to E_{m+n}$. The two associative composites, the two ordinary commutative composites, and the unit composites become the corresponding equal scheme maps after $q^*$, and are equal by faithfulness. Descend the degree-$n$ maps $p^*\mathcal A_n\to E_n$ in the same way: their pullbacks are $\psi_{U,n}$ by the pullback compositor, and the overlaps preserve homogeneous sections. Their sources are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. The descended maps preserve unit and products, again by faithfulness. By [def-trf-etale-graded-module-algebra], these component maps give $\psi:p^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}E_n$ and the products give the graded algebra on $\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}E_n$. The total objects are sheaf coproducts; no claim about commuting global sections with infinite sums is used.

source.place: Tag 084D (lemma-twists-of-structure-sheaf), descent of products and psi, expanded degreewise

proof.text: Let $g:W\to X$ be any scheme test, and let $v:W'=W\times_XU\to W$. This is a surjective etale morphism of schemes by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Put $P_W=W\times_XP$, with $r_W:P_W\to P$. The induced $P_{W'}\to P_W$ is fppf by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. Both $r_W^*E_n$ and the scheme twist $F_{W,n}$ are quasi-coherent, using [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. On this covering identify the first with the pullback of $F_{U,n}$ using $W'\to U$ and the descent trivialization, and the second with $F_{W',n}$ using $W'\to W$. The scheme comparison for $W'\to U$ therefore gives an isomorphism between them on $P_{W'}$. On the double overlap, the two such maps agree by the scheme composition identity of step 3 and the descent datum of step 4. Full faithfulness of [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] descends this map and its inverse to an isomorphism $\lambda_{W,n}:r_W^*E_n\simeq F_{W,n}$. They identify products and $\psi$ since these diagrams do so on $P_{W'}$ and descent is faithful. The scheme underlying $P_W$ is precisely the specified scheme-test comparison of [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests].

source.place: Tag 084D (lemma-twists-of-structure-sheaf), omitted arbitrary-scheme-test verification; Tag 085C (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), twisting-algebra clause

proof.text: For $h:V\to W$ over $X$, compare $\lambda_V$ with $\theta_h\circ h_P^*\lambda_W$, using the compositor of [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition]. After the fppf cover $P_{V\times_XU}\to P_V$, their equality is exactly $\theta_{hk}=\theta_k\circ k_P^*\theta_h$ of step 3, with the atlas pullback maps inserted. Faithfulness of [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] gives equality on $P_V$. The identity and successive-composition assertions follow in the same way from the identity and composition identities already checked on scheme charts. If another family has all the required comparisons, its comparison over $U$ gives isomorphisms to $F_{U,n}$ commuting with $\alpha_n$. Full faithfulness gives unique isomorphisms to $E_n$; they preserve products and $\psi$ because they do so over $P_U$. Step 7 and faithfulness on $P_{W'}\to P_W$ force them to preserve every scheme comparison as well. This proves the asserted uniqueness and independence of the chosen atlas.

source.place: Tag 084D (lemma-twists-of-structure-sheaf), uniqueness and arbitrary pullback verification; Tag 085C, final assertion

proof.text: Finally take $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $C=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}(g^*\mathcal A_n)(W)$. By [lem-sfb-relative-proj-twists-degree-opens], the comparison of step 7 is with the ordinary affine twists of $C$. By [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], on $D_+(f)$ the degree-$n$ module is $(C_f)_n=\{a/f^r:a\in C_{rd+n}\}$, with $C_i=0$ for $i<0$, and the canonical homogeneous section is $a/1$. The multiplication and section normalizations are the fraction formulas already preserved in [lem-sfb-proj-scalar-extension-twist-comparison]: $(a/f^r)(b/f^s)=ab/f^{r+s}$ and $a\mapsto a/1$. Hence every stated chart normalization holds, for negative as well as nonnegative twists. All coverings and coproducts used above are small in the fixed universes; neither the construction nor any cited input requires degree-one generation, finite generation, flatness of a scheme test, separation, or quasi-compactness.
